scope: Isolated POSIX owner runtime with a fake engine, immutable release rollback and artifact identity gate; no production restart or synthetic production generation

implementation.commit_point: after model state, /health, and generation readiness verification
durable_fields: engine executable path, size, and SHA-256
SHA-256 over serve/ and strata_control/ Python runtime files
derived release ID over artifact ID, source-config SHA-256 and launcher SHA-256

contents: serve/ and strata_control/ Python runtime files
chat template, tokenizer module and serve/web assets
exact run config rewritten to the release engine path
identity_policy: artifact_id identifies engine and service-code content
release_id additionally binds the exact source-config digest and launcher digest
identical code with different launch config creates a different release
identical code and config reuse only a fully validated release
staging is fsynced and published with atomic rename

release_policy: verify private ownership, manifest shape, safe relative paths and every digest
refuse tampered engine, service code, assets, config or launcher
restart and startup fallback load the release named by the LKG release_id
the running release and LKG artifact IDs must still match before drain or fallback
restart_policy: reject missing, corrupt, symlinked, digest-mismatched, or running-instance-mismatched LKG
reuse an unchanged regular source file
materialize an owner-private snapshot when the source changed or disappeared
restore the persisted LKG after candidate failure
capture the prior LKG before a fresh owner launches its candidate
fall back once when launch fails, the child exits before ready, or the generation probe fails
complete the same fallback in the owner background when runtime start uses wait=0
do not use the startup-only fallback after a candidate reaches ready
prevent an older generation probe from replacing a newer LKG
record the rollback LKG source digest in the operation journal
report running and candidate artifact IDs in restart plans
refuse drain when the LKG release or running artifact cannot be reproduced exactly
refuse startup fallback when the LKG release or artifact cannot be reproduced exactly
exclude tests, fixtures, CLI files, and tools from the service-code digest

artifact_identity_gate.summary: covered by the full runtime suite
covered: verified launch records engine and Python runtime identity
restart plan reports the running and disk candidate artifacts without stopping
changed code can start only while its prior release remains available for rollback
a fresh owner restores the prior release after the engine is overwritten
a fresh owner cannot roll back to an unverifiable release
test, fixture, CLI, and tools changes do not alter the service artifact
artifact identity is independent of the engine location

release_identity_gate.summary: covered by the full runtime suite
covered: same code with a different config creates a different release
identical code and config reuse the same release
release manifests bind release ID, artifact ID, source digest and config
tampered engine and runtime assets are rejected
the latest LKG release and config are used after a failed restart

lkg_slice.summary: covered by the full runtime suite
covered: first verified launch persists a private LKG
successful restart replaces the LKG
candidate failure rolls back from the persisted LKG
corrupt LKG is rejected before drain
symlinked LKG is rejected before drain
a fresh owner runtime process reads the same LKG
telemetry identity and launch attestation precede /health
a lazy unloaded model passes /health without a generation request
status, service, model, and loaded mismatches reject readiness before generation
runtime start and verify expose health_verified
the operation journal records health_verified
a fresh owner restores the persisted LKG after its candidate exceeds a bound port
the recovered instance becomes the new verified LKG
a successful restart after recovery does not retain the old rollback marker
wait=0 returns starting and the owner completes fallback in the background
the CLI operation journal records rolled_back and rollback_lkg_source_sha256
a missing LKG preserves the original candidate failure
a corrupt LKG is reported as lkg_invalid
a stale generation probe cannot persist or replace the LKG

terminal_suite.regression_found_and_fixed: Immediate SIGTERM after ready publication previously exited -2 for delays 0, 0, 0.01, and 0.05 seconds; ready publication and the serving wait now share the same clean-stop scope, and ten immediate-signal repetitions exited 0

limits: No real model or GPU was restarted
No production generation load was sent
The LKG is not a signed append-only record; it relies on the owner-only runtime directory
The release pins the engine, service Python files, assets, exact run config and launcher
The release store has no retention or garbage collection yet
The LKG does not pin the Python interpreter, installed site-packages, model pack, or shared-library digests
A changed or overwritten release is rejected; it is never silently repaired or replaced
LKG schema 2 is rejected rather than migrated; the first schema 3 launch needs a controlled verified transition
Rollback does not preserve an in-flight HTTP or SSE request
Startup fallback covers a fresh owner candidate that never reaches ready; a candidate that reaches ready and later fails stays outside this path
A real systemd-level restart and real-model startup recovery have not been exercised
Engine smoke, stream smoke, tool smoke, and session restore are not yet one G0B gate
